sentence: Das ist ein schwerer Notfall.
tip: Place the conjugated verb 'ist' in position 2.
translation_en: That is a serious emergency.

sentence: Hoffentlich ist es nicht das Herz!
tip: Put 'ist' right after 'Hoffentlich' in position 2.
translation_en: Hopefully it is not the heart!

sentence: Das ist sicher nicht so schlimm.
tip: Keep 'nicht so schlimm' together at the end of the sentence.
translation_en: That is certainly not so bad.

sentence: Frau Winkler kommt nicht, weil sie Magenschmerzen hat.
tip: In the 'weil' clause, put the conjugated verb 'hat' at the very end.
translation_en: Ms. Winkler is not coming because she has a stomach ache.

sentence: Mein Hausarzt hat heute keine Sprechstunde.
tip: Place the time word 'heute' before 'keine Sprechstunde'.
translation_en: My family doctor has no consultation hours today.

sentence: Deshalb muss ich bis morgen warten.
tip: After 'Deshalb', put the modal verb 'muss' in position 2 and 'warten' at the end.
translation_en: Therefore I have to wait until tomorrow.

sentence: Er will mir nichts sagen, weil meine Krankheit schlimm ist.
tip: Put 'sagen' at the end of the main clause and 'ist' at the end of the 'weil' clause.
translation_en: He doesn't want to tell me anything because my illness is serious.

sentence: Die Untersuchung hat nur fünf Minuten gedauert.
tip: Put 'hat' in position 2 and the participle 'gedauert' at the end.
translation_en: The examination only lasted five minutes.

sentence: Mein Herz ist völlig in Ordnung.
tip: Use the fixed expression 'in Ordnung' at the end.
translation_en: My heart is completely fine.

sentence: Die Ärzte sagen einem nie die Wahrheit.
tip: Dative pronoun 'einem' comes before the accusative object 'die Wahrheit'.
translation_en: The doctors never tell you the truth.

sentence: Deshalb gehe ich gar nicht mehr hin.
tip: The separable prefix 'hin' goes to the very end of the sentence.
translation_en: That's why I don't go there anymore at all.

sentence: Du hast Probleme, weil du zu viel auf deinen Körper hörst.
tip: Put the conjugated verb 'hörst' at the end of the 'weil' clause.
translation_en: You have problems because you listen to your body too much.

sentence: Du musst deinem Hausarzt glauben.
tip: 'glauben' takes the dative object 'deinem Hausarzt' and stands at the end.
translation_en: You have to believe your family doctor.

sentence: Denk doch nicht dauernd an Krankheiten!
tip: Start the informal imperative sentence with the verb 'Denk'.
translation_en: Don't think about illnesses all the time!

sentence: Ich kann heute nicht kommen, weil ich Fieber habe.
tip: End the main clause with 'kommen' and the 'weil' clause with 'habe'.
translation_en: I cannot come today because I have a fever.

sentence: Ich habe Fieber, deshalb kann ich nicht arbeiten.
tip: Put 'kann' immediately after 'deshalb' and 'arbeiten' at the end.
translation_en: I have a fever, so I cannot work.

sentence: Was ist los? Ist alles in Ordnung?
tip: Two short questions to ask if someone is okay.
translation_en: What's wrong? Is everything alright?

sentence: Oh, das tut mir wirklich sehr leid!
tip: Use 'das tut mir ... leid' to express sympathy.
translation_en: Oh, I am really very sorry about that!

sentence: Hoffentlich hast du nichts Schlimmes!
tip: Put the verb 'hast' in position 2 after 'Hoffentlich'.
translation_en: Hopefully you don't have anything serious!

sentence: Ich hoffe, es ist alles in Ordnung.
tip: Start with 'Ich hoffe' followed by the main clause.
translation_en: I hope everything is alright.

sentence: Ich habe große Angst vor Herzkrankheiten.
tip: Use the preposition 'vor' after 'Angst haben'.
translation_en: I am very afraid of heart diseases.

sentence: Hoffentlich muss ich nicht ins Krankenhaus!
tip: Place 'muss' in position 2 after 'Hoffentlich'.
translation_en: Hopefully I don't have to go to the hospital!

sentence: Sie hat Angst vor dem Zahnarzt.
tip: Use the dative article 'dem' after 'vor'.
translation_en: She is afraid of the dentist.

sentence: Er hat große Angst vor Operationen.
tip: Put 'vor Operationen' at the end of the sentence.
translation_en: He is very afraid of operations.

sentence: Gestern hatte ich einen Unfall mit dem Fahrrad.
tip: Put 'hatte' in position 2 after the time word 'Gestern'.
translation_en: Yesterday I had an accident with my bicycle.

sentence: Eine Frau hat den Krankenwagen gerufen.
tip: Put the participle 'gerufen' at the end of the Perfekt sentence.
translation_en: A woman called the ambulance.

sentence: Meine Hand war verletzt und hat stark geblutet.
tip: Put 'geblutet' at the very end of the sentence.
translation_en: My hand was injured and bled heavily.

sentence: Der Notarzt hat gemeint, dass ich ins Krankenhaus muss.
tip: Put the verb 'muss' at the end of the 'dass' clause.
translation_en: The emergency doctor said that I have to go to the hospital.

sentence: In der Notaufnahme hat man meine Hand untersucht.
tip: Put 'hat' in position 2 and 'untersucht' at the end.
translation_en: In the emergency room they examined my hand.

sentence: Ich habe einen Verband bekommen.
tip: Put 'bekommen' at the end of the Perfekt sentence.
translation_en: I got a bandage.

sentence: Ich bin mit dem Taxi nach Hause gefahren.
tip: Place 'mit dem Taxi' before 'nach Hause gefahren'.
translation_en: I took a taxi home.

sentence: Ich gehe in die Apotheke, weil ich Tabletten brauche.
tip: Put the conjugated verb 'brauche' at the end of the 'weil' clause.
translation_en: I am going to the pharmacy because I need pills.

sentence: Er trinkt Kamillentee, weil er Bauchschmerzen hat.
tip: Place 'hat' at the end of the 'weil' clause.
translation_en: He drinks chamomile tea because he has a stomach ache.

sentence: Sie braucht einen Termin, weil sie Zahnschmerzen hat.
tip: Put 'hat' at the very end of the subordinate clause.
translation_en: She needs an appointment because she has a toothache.

sentence: Mein Arzt ist im Urlaub, deshalb fahre ich nach Hause.
tip: Put 'fahre' directly after 'deshalb' before 'ich'.
translation_en: My doctor is on vacation, so I am going home.
